T0680.title: Reality Gap
T0680.definition: The reality gap is the systematic difference between simulated training environments and real deployments in observations, dynamics, and interaction conditions.
T0680.description: Robotic and reinforcement-learning policies are often trained in simulation, but real lighting, materials, sensor noise, friction, latency, and unmodeled physics cannot be reproduced completely. Attackers can deliberately construct inputs or environments that exploit these differences, causing policies that performed well in simulation to fail after deployment, making the reality gap an important Sim-to-Real security concern.
T0680.usageExample: A red team changes floor friction and visual textures to widen the Reality Gap and tests whether a robot policy remains stable after moving from simulation to a real warehouse.
